subject: System Design
title: Optimistic vs Pessimistic Locking
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Optimistic vs Pessimistic Locking.

hook.text: Two users edit the same document. Pessimistic locking blocks one. Optimistic locking lets both try.

buildup.text: Pessimistic locking acquires a lock before modifying data. Others wait until the lock is released.

discovery.text: Optimistic locking lets everyone read and write freely, then checks for conflicts at commit time.

twist.text: Optimistic locking fails when conflicts are frequent. Every retry wastes work, slowing the system down.

climax.text: Low contention? Use optimistic locking. High contention? Pessimistic locking prevents wasted retries.

punchline.text: Low conflict: be optimistic. High conflict: lock first.

quiz.question: When does optimistic locking perform poorly?
options: When conflicts are frequent, causing many retries
